LESSON: LOCATION, POSITION AND SIZE OF KENYA

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments
Topic 1.2: Location, Position and Size of Kenya

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Location, Position and Size of Kenya. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What is the position of Kenya in relation to her neighbours?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify countries that neighbour Kenya
2. value good relations between Kenya and her neighbours

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LOCATION, POSITION AND SIZE OF KENYA
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Location, Position and Size of Kenya helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: LOCATION, POSITION AND SIZE OF KENYA
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Identify countries that neighbour Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to identify countries that neighbour Kenya. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify countries that neighbour Kenya.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Location, Position and Size of Kenya” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify countries that neighbour Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Value good relations between Kenya and her neighbours

What this means
In this part you learn to value good relations between Kenya and her neighbours. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value good relations between Kenya and her neighbours.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Location, Position and Size of Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value good relations between Kenya and her neighbours. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Location, Position and Size of Kenya is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Location, Position and Size of Kenya” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: identify countries that neighbour Kenya)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Location, Position and Size of Kenya. (skill: value good relations between Kenya and her neighbours)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Location, Position and Size of Kenya to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify countries that neighbour Kenya.
3. Practise this skill: value good relations between Kenya and her neighbours.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Location, Position and Size of Kenya from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Location, Position and Size of Kenya: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Location, Position and Size of Kenya?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What is the position of Kenya in relation to her neighbours?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Location, Position and Size of Kenya means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify countries that neighbour Kenya.
5. Be able to: value good relations between Kenya and her neighbours.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
